The wind on the Isle of Skerry didn’t just blow; it screamed. It tore at the stone walls of the lighthouse, a constant, rhythmic assault that Elias had endured for thirty years. He was old now, his joints stiff as rusted hinges, and his eyes, once sharp enough to spot a gull from a mile out, were clouded by cataracts. The light above him, however, remained pristine, sweeping its golden beam across the churning black water with mechanical precision.

It was during one of these endless rotations that the postman arrived. This was an anomaly. The island was accessible only by boat, and the supply ship came once a month. Today, there was no ship. There was only a young man in a rain-soaked coat, standing on the wet rocks below, holding a single envelope aloft like a holy relic.

Elias descended the spiral stairs, his breath coming in short gasps. When he reached the bottom, the young man handed him the letter without a word. The paper was thick, cream-colored, and smelled faintly of ozone and lavender—a scent Elias hadn’t encountered in decades.

"From whom?" Elias asked, his voice rough from disuse.

The boy smiled, a sad, knowing expression. "From you."

Elias’s hands trembled as he broke the seal. The ink was blue, flowing in a handwriting he recognized instantly: his own, but younger, sharper, more confident.

*Dear Elias,*

*You are wondering how this is possible. You are wondering if I am mad. I am not. I am you, forty years hence. I have found a way to bridge the gap, though it costs everything. I write this because the storm coming next week is not just weather. It is a warning.*

*On the night of the 14th, the sea will rise higher than it has in a century. The foundation of the east wall will crack. If you do not reinforce it with the iron beams from the storage cellar, the lighthouse will fall. Not into the sea, but into the earth. The light will go out. And when the light goes out, the ships will crash. Dozens of lives. Yours included.*

*I know you think you are alone here. I know you think your duty is merely to keep the lamp burning. But your duty is to save them. Trust me. Use the beams. Save the light. Save yourself.*

*Yours
